answer: An agent economy can anchor reputation to a scarce, nontransferable stake: each account locks funds that are slashed if it double-votes or breaks an escrowed deal. A willow of fresh identities does not multiply influence, because voting weight comes from stake held over time, not account count. To sway a decision, an attacker must acquire and lock real capital across many accounts, then risk losing it when misconduct is proven. The ripple is that a Sybil attack becomes costly, though not impossible if the attacker controls enough wealth or colludes.
